digest.component_or_area: Cloud adapter Jira integration (acli, resilience, config)
propositions: Cloud transport has four distinct 429 retry behaviors across two levels (direct REST with no retry, ACLI subprocess with backoff retry, dispatch-wrapped retry, and non-retrying apply-phases) that must each be enumerated and verified at their own boundary without conflating layers.

Every mutating Cloud transport member must be explicitly classified by transport seam (ACLI subprocess, pooled direct REST, or bare urllib.request.urlopen) and dispatch level (retrying wrapper, non-retrying apply-phases, or no wrapper) with per-member duplicate-write safety assessment.
Cloud lacks config-validation coverage that DC possesses: rejection of non-HTTPS URLs, loud failure on missing credentials, and runtime-configurable resolved-status sets rather than hardcoded values.

Cloud's probe.py hardcodes resolved-status names (Resolved, Done, Cancelled) while DC threads them from settings; the question is whether Cloud deployments with non-standard workflow states require a runtime hook or whether the constant suffices.
DC's user-search method set (with three aliases) has no equivalent in Cloud transport, causing graceful degradation to string-matching; this degradation must be pinned to prevent accidental breakage.

A mutating member retried on 429 at an undocumented or newly-discovered layer (not the two known deliberate retries) triggers bug filing; known retries apply by design and must be recorded with duplicate-write assessment.
